sar.narrative: On 2016-11-06, customer C09623 utilized card C09623-K2 for two transaction(s) totalling $570.05, including a $549.96 transaction, in person under product code W and billed in region 204.0, and when contacted regarding this activity, no reply within 24 hours was received, an assumption recorded in the case file because no cardholder replies were available to this investigation. During this same period, 3 of the card-detail match flags M1-M9 came back F on the $549.96 transaction, step-up authentication was not completed, and connected components over the device-sharing graph placed card C09623-K2 in a bounded component of 2 cards, C00266-K1, linked transitively through device profiles each used by no more than 8 cards, indicating a common actor operating across more than one cardholder. The activity is suspicious because it is consistent with known fraud pattern 5 for account takeover, which involves mixed-channel activity inconsistent with the cardholder, often with device and match-flag anomalies, pointing to stolen credentials rather than a stolen number, and the $549.96 transaction amount is 8.0x this card's median and above its 95th percentile, though large outliers appear on 16% of cleared alarms and 6% of confirmed fraud because confirmed fraud tends to stay inside the cardholder's normal range to avoid attention. The probability of fraud was assessed at 0.76, and the exposure was $570.05, while external email-domain intelligence classified 'yahoo.com' as a free webmail address that carries no weight, and the 5 closed cases whose transaction most resembles this one, CC-1342, CC-4201, CC-5496, CC-4781, and CC-1596, all closed as confirmed fraud (account takeover, out of region use) and 0 cleared. Because the evidence conflicts and the exposure exceeds $500, policy rule R8 requires escalation, and under policy rule R6 the shared origin of C00266-K1 requires naming the shared element, recommending CREATE_CASE and FILE_REPORT, and MONITOR_CONNECTED_CARDS, and under policy rule R4 the pending authorisation must be declined and the card monitored. Accordingly, the matter was escalated to a fraud analyst, an internal investigation case was opened, the cards sharing the same origin were placed under monitoring, and the pending authorisation was declined.
